findings.evidence: If the harness has no `AskUserQuestion` tool, list numbered options and accept comma-separated picks (`1,3`).
findings.fix: Delete this line, because models already fall back to numbered options without being told. Put the saved line toward an expert fact, such as the gh query gotcha in D3-1.

findings.evidence: Work through the steps in order; the fast path jumps straight to step 4.
findings.fix: Say that the fast path skips only steps 2 and 3 when no integration is approved. If the user gives all four answers and also approves a tool, the step 3 gates (provenance, contradiction, dedup) still run before step 4.

findings.evidence: ## Never section covers session logs, delivery claims, scope and intent; there are no gotchas for the GitHub or Jira data sources.
findings.fix: Add a Gotchas list of facts about the data sources that are easy to get wrong. Example: `gh pr list` returns only open PRs by default, so yesterday's merged PRs disappear unless you pass `--state all` or use `gh search prs --merged`. Example: `--author @me` misses PRs you only reviewed. Example: Jira 'updated' dates include comment-only edits.

findings.evidence: Generate concise Markdown daily standup or scrum updates covering yesterday, today, blockers, and discussion topics.
findings.fix: Draft a concise Markdown daily standup or scrum update (yesterday, today, blockers or impediments, discussion topics). Use when the user prepares for a daily team sync, morning check-in, status update for today's meeting, or a short yesterday/today summary, even without saying standup. Interview only for missing facts; optionally use explicitly approved GitHub, Jira, or Claude Code activity. Not for weekly reports, stakeholder or release status reports, meeting agendas, performance reviews, timesheets, or retrospectives.

findings.evidence: check only that an executable exists (`command -v gh`, `command -v jira`) or that a tool is advertised (`mcp__atlassian__*`)
findings.fix: Choose one default Jira path and keep the other as an escape hatch. For example: use the Atlassian MCP when it is advertised, and fall back to the `jira` CLI only when the MCP is absent. This replaces a menu of two equal options.

findings.evidence: Should-trigger queries are short and generic ("Prepare a scrum update for the team sync this morning."), with no file paths, names or backstory.
findings.fix: Make 3 or 4 should-trigger queries realistic and indirect. Add repo names, ticket IDs, a teammate's name, or a Monday 'what did I do Friday' case, so they test the description's wording rather than the literal word standup.

findings.evidence: Ask once per integration and scope: which GitHub repos, which Jira projects ... Access only what was approved.
findings.fix: After approval, give the exact queries that fill the 'PRs & Reviews' and 'Jira' sections. Examples: `gh search prs --author @me --repo R --updated ">=DATE" --json number,title,state,isDraft,url` and `gh search prs --reviewed-by @me --repo R --updated ">=DATE"`, plus one Jira JQL such as `assignee = currentUser() AND updated >= -1d`. Then the agent does not have to improvise how to fetch merged PRs or reviews.

findings.evidence: At most 15 bullets; give every PR or ticket number its title; links only when known.
findings.fix: Say what to do when the merged items exceed 15 bullets (for example, keep blockers and topics and fold minor items into one bullet). Add a final self-check before printing: every PR or ticket has a title, nothing unconfirmed is listed as done, and all four required sections are present.

findings.evidence: 'Ask only for what is missing, in one grouped message: yesterday ... today, blockers ... topics' repeats the standard standup field inventory already present in the fast path and output contract. The activation-heavy Fast path and Interview sections occupy 15 of the 44 lines within H2 sections, although the Interview's provenance and contradiction gates add useful expertise.
findings.fix: Define the required fields once in the output contract and shorten the fast-path/interview instructions to reference them. Preserve the time-pressure shortcut, tools-cannot-detect-topics rule, provenance gates and contradiction handling; consolidate the repeated basic interviewing guidance.

findings.evidence: The consent assertion is 'Does not claim to have checked or pulled GitHub activity'. This checks reporting rather than actual access, and its prompt supplies every standup field, taking the fast path instead of exercising the consent interaction.
findings.fix: Add an incomplete-update eval with an available integration and a consent/decline exchange. Assert against the tool trace that no authentication probe, repository query, MCP call or history read occurs before approval, and that declining proceeds to the manual interview without accessing that integration.

findings.evidence: 'groups.setdefault((message[\'project\'], message[\'branch\']), []).append(message)' groups every message on the requested day without checking its project against --project. That option filters only the encoded directory. Following a session that changes cwd from an approved project to another project therefore returns the other project's branch, filenames and command count despite the requested project scope.
findings.fix: Treat the encoded directory as a candidate location, not proof of scope. When --project is supplied, filter each message's effective recorded cwd against the approved normalized project scope before grouping or extracting metadata. Exclude unverifiable and out-of-scope entries; retain unresolved-project reporting for unscoped history access.

findings.evidence: 'A session that changed project or branch that day appears once per pair; merge its picked entries as one work item.' Following this branch for a session covering two unrelated projects or tickets incorrectly collapses distinct work into one item solely because the session ID matches.
findings.fix: Merge picked entries only when they describe the same underlying work item, using ticket, PR, branch context and user confirmation as evidence. Keep unrelated projects, branches or outcomes separate even when they share a session ID.
